## Finding

In an `#if`, each of `__has_attribute`, `__has_cpp_attribute`, `__has_c_attribute`, and
`__has_builtin` stops sdcpp with an internal compiler error, for every name. The three attribute
macros stop in `get_identifier`, and `__has_builtin` stops in `names_builtin_p`. This was
reproduced for mcs51 with the reporter's `annotations.h` and with the program from bug #3844.
`__has_builtin` is not in the ticket.

## Cause

sdcpp is the preprocessor of GCC 13 without the compiler proper. `support/cpp/gcc/cc1_dummies.cc`
defines the compiler's functions as dummies that end in an internal compiler error.
`c_common_has_attribute` in `support/cpp/gcc/c-family/c-lex.cc` converts the attribute name to an
identifier tree with `get_identifier`, and for a name with a prefix it calls `build_tree_list`.
The lookup that would use the tree is inside `#if 0` in trunk. `c_common_has_builtin` calls
`names_builtin_p`.

## Fix

Both patches change `c-lex.cc` only. The first one puts the conversion of the name inside `#if 0`
as well and removes two debug messages that the function writes to stderr. The three attribute
macros then check their syntax and give 0 for every name. The second patch makes
`c_common_has_builtin` compare the name with a list of two names. It is a separate patch so that it
can be left out, and `__has_builtin` then keeps the internal error.

## Decision

The attribute macros give 0 for every name, including standard attributes such as `nodiscard`,
`deprecated`, `maybe_unused`, `fallthrough`, and `noreturn`. C23 specifies a nonzero value for
`__has_c_attribute` when the implementation supports the attribute. sdcc implements none. Its
grammar gives warning 284, "unknown attribute ignored", for every attribute name, and sdcc reports
a syntax error for `[[nodiscard]] int f (void);`. With 0, headers that ask before they use an
attribute compile. With the C23 values, such headers would use `[[...]]` and get the warning or
the syntax error.

`__has_builtin` gives 1 for `__builtin_offsetof` and `__builtin_unreachable` and 0 for every other
name. sdcc has these two on every port. `__builtin_offsetof` is a keyword in `src/SDCC.lex`, and
`initBuiltIns` in `src/SDCCsymt.c` creates `__builtin_unreachable`. The list in the patch does not
depend on the port, so the built-in functions of single ports get 0. Examples are
`__builtin_memcpy` on the z80 family and `__builtin_memset` on ds390. Code that asks first uses its
fallback on these ports. mcs51 has no built-in functions of its own.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-3715.c` uses the four macros in `#if` lines, among them the sequence
from `annotations.h` and the program from bug #3844. It uses `__builtin_offsetof` and
`__builtin_unreachable` when `__has_builtin` gives 1 for them. Without the patches sdcc does not
compile the test. With them it passes on the host, the six mcs51 variants, stm8, and ucz80, and it
compiles with `--std-c23`. No other regression test changes size for mcs51 in the small model.

A name with a prefix, as in `__has_c_attribute(gnu::unused)`, gives 0 with `--std-c23`. In the
default mode `::` is not a token, and sdcpp reports an ordinary error about the closing
parenthesis. Uses of the macros with wrong syntax also give ordinary errors.

## Related

Bug #3844 reports the same failure for `__has_attribute` and is fixed by the first patch. The
fourth comment of this ticket reports it for `__has_c_attribute`.
